lines.trans: Oh Cindy, good timing—I was just looking for you anyway. You know Jinny, right?
I barely watch television.
She has boundless potential so our agency signed her—since 2 Days & 1 Night is preempted this week, let us knock out this schedule.
How many appearances is this packed into two days?! Wait—am I appearing alongside that girl from earlier?
Yes, our Jinny sings well, yet she still has zero broadcast experience—go on together and coach her like an older sister.
Are you telling me right now to go pave the stage for her and do trashy bookings like these?!

words.gloss: to roll out the mat for

lines.trans: Yes, that is right—exactly that.
If you treat me like this, you will keep making me have second thoughts when contract renewal comes around.
Second thoughts? Go right ahead! It is an important decision, so you ought to weigh every option.
Except do you renew a contract all by yourself? I should entertain second thoughts of my own.

meanings.note: Used as noun + subject (가능성이).

examples.text: 가능성이 무궁무진한 아이라 우리 회사에서 영입했어. 이번 주 1박 결방이라며, 자 이거 좀 하자.
examples.trans: She has boundless potential so our agency signed her—since 2 Days & 1 Night is preempted this week, let us knock out this schedule.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (noun).

examples.text: 정권 바뀌면 바꿀 게 한두 가지가 아니에요.
examples.trans: When leadership changes, there is way more than one or two things you have to change.
Here the word for 'kinds, items' is key.

meanings.note: Adverb meaning 'together', often pronounced 가치.

examples.trans: Let's go together.
Let's go together. (2)

meanings.note: General-purpose counter noun used with native Korean determiners (한 개, 두 개, 세 개).

examples.trans: How many do you need?
I bought three loaves of bread.

meanings.note: Colloquial contraction of 그 아이 ('that child/kid'); used only for younger people or close peers.

examples.trans: Are you close with her?
He is late every day.

related.gloss: this kid / he or she (near speaker)
that kid / he or she (over there)

meanings.note: Bound noun often contracted to 거 in everyday speech.

examples.trans: This is my bag.
Because I think I'm late.

meanings.note: Used as broadcasting noun (결방?).

examples.trans: A preemption? Our broadcast is preempted?
Rather than calling it a preemption…

meanings.note: Pairs with 나다 (결정 나다, 'a decision is reached') or 하다 (결정하다, 'to decide').

examples.trans: A decision hasn't been reached yet.
I have to make an important decision.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (noun).

examples.text: 보다 보면 재미가 있겠지, 승찬이가 지금은 경험이 부족해서 그렇지.
examples.trans: Keep watching and it will get funny—Seung-chan just lacks experience for now.
Here the word for 'experience' is key.

meanings.note: refers to something known to both speakers or near the listener

examples.trans: That movie was really fun.
What is that person's name?

meanings.note: Colloquial contraction of 그것

examples.trans: Where did you buy that?
That is a really good idea.

meanings.note: dummy

examples.trans: dummy trans 1
dummy trans 2

그러다.gloss: to say so; to do so

meanings.en: to say so; to speak like that
meanings.note: contracted from 그러하다; often follows quoted speech

meanings.en: to do so; to act like that

examples.trans: Who said that?
That friend also said they are going together.

meanings.note: Colloquial contraction of 그런데; introduces a contrast or obstacle.
Used to shift the topic in conversation.

examples.trans: By the way, what time is it now?
I want to go. But I don't have time.

깔아주다.gloss: to roll out the mat for

meanings.en: to roll out the mat for
meanings.note: Used as purposive -러 (깔아주러).

examples.text: 나더러 지금 걔 판 깔아주러 나가서 이딴 거 하란 거예요?
examples.trans: Are you telling me right now to go pave the stage for her and do trashy bookings like these?!
Let us do that (to roll out the mat for) right away.

meanings.note: Plain first-person singular pronoun used with friends, younger people, or subordinates; contracts to 난 with -는 and becomes 내가 before -가.

examples.trans: I'm going to stay home today.
I'll go first.

나가다.gloss: to go out, to step outside

meanings.en: to go out, to step outside, to leave a room
meanings.note: 나- ('out') + 가다 ('to go')

examples.trans: Let's step outside for a moment and talk.
He went out of the conference room.
Do you have time today?
Where are you going?

meanings.note: Used only with close friends, younger people, or children

examples.trans: Do you know any of my songs?
The topic of song came up during this shoot.

meanings.note: Used for time or order.

examples.trans: Let's meet next time.
The next station is Seoul Station.

meanings.note: Often combined with 하다 ('to replace') or 가능하다 ('to be replaceable').

examples.text: 이 표현은 다른 말로 대체할 수 있어요.
examples.trans: This expression can be replaced with another word.
I found an appropriate replacement expression.

meanings.note: Used after a time period.

examples.trans: for three days
for three days (2)

meanings.note: Takes a complement marked with 이/가.

examples.trans: I want to become a doctor.
It has already become 12 o'clock.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (noun).

examples.text: 리허설 중간에도 저렇게 딴생각을 하고 있으시구나, 쟤 왜 안 비켜!
examples.trans: Daydreaming right in the middle of rehearsal—wait, why is she not stepping out of the way!
Here the word for 'daydreaming, other thoughts' is key.

meanings.note: Used as resultative -게 (딴생각하게).

examples.text: 이러시면 저 재계약 때 자꾸 딴생각하게 돼요.
examples.trans: If you treat me like this, you will keep making me have second thoughts when contract renewal comes around.
Let us do that (to have second thoughts) right away.

meanings.note: Often used as a bound noun after -(으)ㄹ to mean 'when' or 'while'.

examples.trans: Call me when you have time.
I lived in this neighborhood when I was young.

meanings.note: Action of coming together with someone.

examples.trans: I meet a friend.
Let's meet tomorrow.

맞다.gloss: to be right, to be correct

meanings.note: Used to confirm facts or answers.

meanings.en: to fit, to suit, to match
meanings.note: E.g., 사이즈가 맞다 ('the size fits').

examples.trans: Yes, that's my phone number.
These shoes fit my feet perfectly.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (num).

examples.text: 너희는 사람이 몇인데 그걸 아무도 못 봤냐?
examples.trans: With so many staffers on your team, how did nobody catch that?
Here the word for 'so many, yet' is key.

meanings.note: Used as four-character adnominal (무궁무진한).

examples.text: 가능성이 무궁무진한 아이라 우리 회사에서 영입했어. 이번 주 1박 결방이라며, 자 이거 좀 하자.
examples.trans: She has boundless potential so our agency signed her—since 2 Days & 1 Night is preempted this week, let us knock out this schedule.

meanings.note: Refers to both the act of broadcasting and the aired program itself.

examples.trans: That program airs on Sunday evening.

examples.trans: Huh? Where is my phone?

meanings.note: Everyday spoken contraction of 이것.

examples.trans: How much is this?

examples.trans: Are you telling me right now to go pave the stage for her and do trashy bookings like these?!

이러다.gloss: to do this, to act like this

meanings.en: to do this, to act like this
meanings.note: Contracted from 이러하다.

examples.trans: Why are you acting like this?
Please don't do this.

meanings.note: Used before time nouns like 이번 주 (this week)

meanings.note: Humble first-person singular pronoun used in polite speech.

meanings.note: Contraction of 조금
Used in 이번 주 (this week), 다음 주 (next week)

meanings.note: Used as loanword + -도 (코치도).

examples.text: 응, 우리 지니 노래만 잘하지 아직 방송 경험은 없잖니. 네가 같이 나가서 언니처럼 코치도 해주고.

meanings.en: to do, to perform, to hold

examples.trans: What are you doing right now?

I want to even try right now.
How about trying to even try together tomorrow?

meanings.note: Compound of 하다 (to do) and 주다 (to give).

examples.trans: Please help me (do helping for me).
Please do this for me.

meanings.note: Softens a question or expresses uncertainty.

examples.trans: Did you happen to film this just now too?
Do you happen to have time?
I ate alone today.
I can do it well by myself too.

meanings.note: Can also function as a noun

examples.trans: My office is close to home.
